Random sampling counters automation bias by ensuring that not all investigations are based solely on high-risk signals generated by algorithms. By incorporating a random sample into the fraud detection process, inspectors are encouraged to critically evaluate cases rather than relying blindly on algorithmic results. This approach helps to monitor and mitigate risks of discrimination, as it allows for a more balanced selection of cases for investigation.

In relation to the AI Act duties for high-risk providers, the use of random sampling aligns with the requirement for these providers to identify and mitigate reasonably foreseeable risks, including potential discrimination. The AI Act mandates that high-risk AI systems must comply with specific requirements for control and transparency, and employing random sampling can serve as a control tool to ensure that the algorithm does not disproportionately affect certain groups, thereby fulfilling part of the obligations set forth in the AI Act.
